tolerance_classes.EXACT_BYTES: files / serialized outputs byte-identical (sha256 equal); not used by this contract except where an observable says so
tolerance_classes.EXACT_VALUE: integers, strings, enums, booleans, statuses, error codes, schema shape, and floats that are copied (not computed): equal (floats compared by value, -0.0 == 0.0)
tolerance_classes.ULP_BOUNDED: |rust - py| <= k_ulp * ulp(py) OR |rust - py| <= r_rel * |py| OR |rust - py| <= a_abs, with k_ulp / r_rel / a_abs fixed per observable below (an absent clause is not applied). The relative clause is scaled by |py|, NOT by max(1, |py|) as in the template's proposal: the observables span 1e-12 .. 1e17, so an absolute floor of r_rel would accept nonsense for small quantities; scaling by |py| is strictly tighter for |py| < 1 and identical otherwise. ulp(py) = 2^(floor(log2|py|) - 52) (py = 0: smallest subnormal)
tolerance_classes.EXACT_STREAM: not used (no RNG in either implementation; the harness RNG only draws input vectors)

tolerance_basis.independence: fixed from an a priori floating-point analysis of the two registered algorithms on the frozen inputs, before any Rust code or Python-vs-Rust comparison existed; the only measurements used are properties of the inputs and of the reference environment (max |ln rho| of the frozen CSV = 25.42; pandas parses the CSV to the correctly rounded doubles; numpy dispatches AVX512 SIMD float64 log / exp)
tolerance_basis.which_operations_differ: Rust (glibc libm via std) and CPython math (glibc libm) evaluate math.exp / math.log / math.sqrt identically; IEEE basic operations in the same order are identical; np.interp is compiled for the X86_V2 baseline (no FMA contraction possible) and is reproduced operation by operation. The only differing operation is np.log(d.rho) on the 76-node column, which numpy evaluates with its AVX512 SIMD loop (<= 4 ulp, numpy's documented SIMD transcendental bound) while Rust uses glibc log (< 1 ulp)
tolerance_basis.bound_rho: node log difference <= 5 ulp(25.42) = 1.78e-14; np.interp is an affine combination with weights in [0, 1] (+ <= 2 roundings of 3.55e-15 each); math.exp then math.log add <= 1 ulp(25.42); the F10.7 combination (1-w) log a + w log b adds <= 2 roundings; the final exp turns the absolute log difference into a relative one: |rho_rust / rho_py - 1| <= 3.4e-14
tolerance_basis.bound_derived: fO, fN2, fO2, T: identical inputs and operations (expected bit-identical); m_mean, n, flux, p_ambient, n_O: rho's bound plus <= 4 roundings (<= 1e-15)
tolerance_basis.registered: r_rel = 1e-12 (scale |py|) for every interpolated / derived float: ~29x above the a priori bound and 5e3 below the 9-significant-digit storage resolution of the CSV (5e-9), so no data, interpolation or formula defect can hide under it; k_ulp = 4 (template proposal) for V, which is a correctly rounded sqrt of a correctly rounded quotient in both implementations

documented_divergence.statement: Rust never reads ABEP_ATMOSPHERE / ABEP_ALLOW_TABLE_ATMOSPHERE and has no live-NRLMSIS or built-in-table branch; its API takes only (alt_km, solar), so Python's non-scenario arguments (ap, date, lat_deg, lon_deg, orbit_average=False, use_msis=True) have no Rust counterpart
Rust verifies the CSV and JSON sha256 against config/MANIFEST.json -> physics_model_set_v1 and the sidecar sha256_16 prefix; Python _frozen() reads them unverified
documented_divergence.disposition: required by A9.29 sec. 6 (hash verification) and CLAUDE.md rules 1, 3; scored by RF-A-03 with the registered divergent outcome

documented_divergence.statement: Python atmosphere() memoizes on round(alt_km, 3) but evaluates at the unrounded alt_km, so in one process a later call whose altitude rounds to an earlier key returns the earlier result (history-dependent; CLAUDE.md rule 5 requires caches to be pure functions of their keys). Rust has no memo
documented_divergence.disposition: the harness clears _MSIS_CACHE before every reference call, so every reference output is the pure evaluation; recorded as a PYTHON_REFERENCE observation for its own governance, not changed here

documented_divergence.statement: orbital_velocity with a non-finite altitude: Python returns nan / 0.0 / -0.0; Rust refuses with OUT_OF_DOMAIN
documented_divergence.disposition: fail-closed (CLAUDE.md rule 3); scored by DE-A-13..15 with the registered divergent outcome

documented_divergence.statement: Rust takes f64 inputs only; a Python int input is echoed as int in the result dict

It is NOT physics validation.
